questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's weight pulls it forward in curves, making it hard to turn. Slow down before entering a curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving 45 mph or faster, signal to turn ____ before you begin the turn.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 200 feet before turning or changing lanes when driving faster than 45 mph. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, keep a minimum distance of:
questions.explanation: More distance between vehicles gives you more time to react. Keep two seconds of distance in normal weather and traffic. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way and must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop.
Use crosswalks only if they are convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: If your vehicle skids, you should:

options.text: Turn sharply in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your vehicle skids. Steer in the same direction the back of your vehicle is sliding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of opposite traffic are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead is low. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that drivers must always obey. Right turns are not permitted where this sign is posted.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. This means:

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge shows where the road boundary is. When the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As your speed increases, you see less around you. You must stay extra alert for hazards.

questions.question: A car is heading straight at you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right to escape. Don't steer left—if the other driver swerves at the last second, you'll still crash. Brake hard and steady. Slowing down even a little will reduce the impact.

questions.question: If your license was already suspended and reinstated, how many points will cause another suspension within three years?
questions.explanation: When you get traffic violations, points go on your record. If you get eight points on a license that was already suspended and reinstated, your license will be suspended again. A second suspension lasts six months. A third suspension lasts 12 months.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign means no passing zone. This shape is only used for this warning.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When you approach an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look all directions, then go.

questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to cars coming from your right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Take your foot off the gas, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic going the same direction.

questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but solid lines are not for crossing. You may cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: When visibility gets worse, what is your first action?
questions.explanation: Your first action when visibility decreases is to slow down. This keeps you safe in bad road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through it means the action is not allowed. In this case, a right turn is not allowed.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph needs up to ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need much longer distances to stop than cars going at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph may need almost 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two tracks side by side, watch for a second train on the other track after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams comes toward you, look toward the ____ side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has bright high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded and lets you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes to help you merge. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into that opening.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What best keeps you and others safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to alert people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is hard because drivers cannot see directly behind their vehicles. Before backing up, walk around the back of the vehicle to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks with flammable liquids must stop at railroad crossings. Be prepared to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.
